![Craft Alert logo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/F0rty-Tw0/CraftAlert/master/.github/screenshots/logo.png)

# Craft Alert

Craft Alert watches Trade chat for people asking for something one of your characters can craft, then shows a toast so you can greet them with one click. Open each profession window once and it knows your recipes across every character on the account. It never whispers on its own: every message comes from your click or keybind. Works on Retail, WoW: Forever, and the Classic flavors (Era, TBC Anniversary, Wrath, Cata, MoP) from one folder.

## Screenshots

A toast beside the launcher ring when someone asks for something your alt can craft:

![Toast for an item link](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/F0rty-Tw0/CraftAlert/master/.github/screenshots/toast.png)

![Toast for a profession request](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/F0rty-Tw0/CraftAlert/master/.github/screenshots/toast-chat.png)

The leads window, with the selected request, who can craft it and the greeting that Greet sends:

![Leads window](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/F0rty-Tw0/CraftAlert/master/.github/screenshots/leads-window.png)

Hover the day's counts for the last 7 days:

![Last 7 days of leads](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/F0rty-Tw0/CraftAlert/master/.github/screenshots/stats-week.png)

Settings, opened with the gear on the window's title bar. The Crafters page picks a main crafter per profession and mutes recipes:

![Settings, Crafters page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/F0rty-Tw0/CraftAlert/master/.github/screenshots/settings-crafters.png)

The same mute switch sits on each recipe in your profession window: click the speaker to mute or unmute it.

![Speakers in the profession window](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/F0rty-Tw0/CraftAlert/master/.github/screenshots/profession-window.png)

With WhisperMessenger installed, the leads move into its Craft Alert tab:

![Leads in WhisperMessenger](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/F0rty-Tw0/CraftAlert/master/.github/screenshots/whisper-messenger.png)

## What it does

- Listens in Trade and Services where the game has them (General, LookingForGroup, Guild and Communities can be turned on) for requests such as "LF plate belt", "WTB [item link]" or "LF enchanter".
- Shows a toast beside its launcher ring with what the customer wants and which of your characters can craft it. Left-click greets, shift-click lets you edit the greeting first, ctrl-click opens an empty whisper, right-click dismisses.
- Opens the greeting in the chat box for you to send instead when you are AFK, greet more than six times a minute, greet the same lead twice, or click a lead that just appeared.
- Keeps every open request in a leads window: the list on the left, the selected request in full on the right, with Greet, Whisper and Dismiss buttons.
- Counts the requests you saw, greeted and got a reply from each day, and tells you what came in while you were AFK.
- Picks the best of your characters for each request, and lets you choose a main crafter per profession.
- Turns itself off in dungeons, raids, battlegrounds, arenas and delves.
- With WhisperMessenger installed, the leads move into a WhisperMessenger tab and greetings open as WhisperMessenger conversations.

## Install

1. Download Craft Alert and unzip it.
2. Put the `CraftAlert` folder in the `Interface/AddOns` folder of your game version, for example `World of Warcraft/_retail_/Interface/AddOns`.
3. Start the game (or `/reload`) and check that Craft Alert is enabled in the AddOns list.
4. On each character, open each crafting profession window once, so Craft Alert learns its recipes. The login chat line tells you which professions are still missing.

## Commands

- `/ca` (or `/craftalert`) shows or hides the leads window.
- `/ca config` opens the settings. The gear on the leads window's title bar opens them too.
- `/ca test <a trade line>` runs the line through Craft Alert as if someone had said it in Trade, prints what matched and why, and makes a test lead you can click. Test greetings send nothing. Add `as <class>` to set the test customer's class (`/ca test as warrior LF belt`), or use `/ca test reply` to fake the customer's reply.
- `/ca perf` times the chat scan and reports every minute until you run it again.

Key bindings for greeting the latest lead, dismissing it, and showing or hiding the leads window are under Craft Alert in the game's Key Bindings.

## Linked accounts

Craft Alert can name crafters from your other Battle.net account, so a request on this account can be greeted for your alt over there. Both accounts need the same game version.

1. On the account that has the crafters, open Settings → Linked accounts and click the Export string box. It selects the whole string; press Ctrl+C.
2. On the other account, open Settings → Linked accounts, paste the string into the Import string box with Ctrl+V and click Import.
3. The page lists the characters you imported and when. Importing again later updates them and keeps your choices for them (on or off, main crafter).

## Moving from CraftScan (Retail)

1. Keep CraftScan enabled for one login.
2. At login Craft Alert offers once to import this account's CraftScan characters, recipes and greetings. Click Import. Recipes CraftScan isn't scanning come in muted, and anything Craft Alert already has stays as it is.
3. Missed the offer or clicked Decline? Settings → Linked accounts → Import from CraftScan does the same.
4. Once the import reports how many characters and recipes came in (in chat, or on the page), you can disable CraftScan.

## Privacy

Craft Alert reads chat inside the game and keeps what it learns in its own saved variables on your computer. Nothing leaves the game except what you choose to send: the greeting whisper, and just before each greeting Craft Alert sends for you (not ones it opens in the chat box), a hidden addon message to the same player (`Q:CraftAlert`, under the `robots.txt` prefix) so their addons can tell the whisper came from an addon. The Linked accounts string goes only where you paste it.

# Changelog

Player-friendly release notes for Craft Alert.

## [Unreleased]

## [1.0.5] - 2026-11-12

- Clicking a lead's alert on the Whisper Messenger button now also looks up the customer, so their level, class and zone show in the chat. Needs the latest Whisper Messenger.

## [1.0.4] - 2026-11-08

- With the latest Whisper Messenger, Craft Alert now appears by name in its "Allow addon integration" list, with its own checkbox. Needs the latest Whisper Messenger.
- Fixed: in Whisper Messenger's narrow window, the lead list no longer hides leads behind its background.
- With the latest Whisper Messenger, Craft Alert's page stays on one screen while the window is compact, even if you drag it wider.

## [1.0.3] - 2026-11-07

- With Whisper Messenger's Window animation turned off, Craft Alert's pages in the Whisper Messenger window no longer slide. Needs the latest Whisper Messenger.
- Fixed: Clicking an alert on the Whisper Messenger button to send your greeting no longer opens the messenger when its "Auto-open on outgoing whisper" option is off. Needs the latest Whisper Messenger.
- In Whisper Messenger's compact window, Craft Alert's page now fits the narrow window: tap a lead to see its details, and use the back arrow to return.

## [1.0.2] - 2026-11-06

- WoW: Forever and Classic: while you stand in a capital, a request that names only another capital ("LF enchanter in Org" when you're in Undercity) no longer alerts. Short names like org, uc, tb, sw or if count after "in", "at", "to", "from", "near" or "@"; full city names count anywhere. Turn it off with "Hide askers in another capital" in Settings → General.
- WoW: Forever and Classic: left-click a lead to see where its asker is. Craft Alert asks /who quietly, without opening the Who window, and the lead shows "in Orgrimmar", in red when that's another capital.
- New greeting tag `{city}`: "I'm in Undercity." while you stand in a capital, nothing anywhere else. New default greetings on Forever and Classic end with it. Greetings you already have stay as they are: add `{city}` yourself, or clear a greeting's box in Settings → Greetings to get the new default.

## [1.0.1] - 2026-11-05

- Characters on another realm no longer get alerts or greetings unless Craft Alert knows they're connected to your realm. To turn one back on, pick it on the Crafters page and turn on "Listen for this character".
- Names show a realm only when it matters, and never on WoW: Forever.
- The main crafter is now one per profession in each group of realms.

## [1.0.0] - 2026-10-30

- First release. Craft Alert watches chat for people asking for something one of your characters can craft and lets you greet them with one click. One folder works on Retail, WoW: Forever and the Classic flavors (Era, TBC Anniversary, Wrath, Cata, Mists of Pandaria).
- Open each profession window once and Craft Alert knows that character's recipes, across every character on the account. On Era and TBC that includes Enchanting's craft window.
- Recipes from older expansions start muted: Craft Alert alerts only for the newest expansion's recipes of each profession, and when you first open a profession after a new expansion it switches to that one (your own mutes for that profession are replaced, and a chat line says so). "Only " on the Crafters page does the same on demand.
- A recipe you learn while playing matches right away. On Classic it matches by name until you next open its profession window, which stores it for good.
- Reading profession windows and building the recipe list happen in the background, a little each frame, without stalling the game.
- Craft Alert listens in Trade and Services by default; General, LookingForGroup, Guild and Communities can be turned on where the game has them. "Only where Trade chat exists" keeps it listening wherever you have the Trade channel.
- Requests are matched by item and recipe links, written item names, slot and armor words ("LF plate belt"), and profession words ("LF enchanter", "bs", "jc", "jewelcraft", "leatherwork", "insc"). A line needs a request word: LF, LFC, LFRC, WTB, WTC, need, looking, anyone and a few more by default. Edit the request words and add your own slang in Settings → Keywords.
- "Recraft", "recrafter" and "recrafting" work like "crafter", "leg" works like "legs", "off hand" and "off-hand" name the off hand, and "enchs" names Enchanting.
- A line that names two slots matches either one.
- A request that names a slot without an armor type ("LF belt", "LF head crafter") uses the asker's class, enchant requests excepted: a warrior's request alerts only for plate, a mage's only for cloth. On Forever and Classic the class is read as max level (a level 30 hunter counts as mail).
- A bare "LF crafter" alerts the profession that makes the asker's armor: Blacksmithing for plate, Leatherworking for mail and leather, Tailoring for cloth. It needs profession-word alerts on, and only works for a line that names nothing else: "LF crafter for flask" or "LF crafter, ring" makes no armor guess.
- Ads are left alone: lines with WTS, LFW or "selling", lines with "/w me" but none of LF, LFC, LFRC, WTB or WTC, and "LF work" (but not "LF work order") make no alert. "Trinket" on its own picks no profession; name the trinket instead.
- A toast pops up beside the launcher, on the side facing the middle of the screen, when someone asks for something you can craft. It says what they want and which of your characters can craft it (an alt by name, in its class colour), shows their whole message with item and recipe links you can hover, and what matched in its tooltip. Left-click to greet them, shift-click to edit the greeting first, ctrl-click for an empty whisper, right-click to dismiss; a click on a link only opens the link. A newer request replaces the shown one and counts "+N more". Dragging the toast moves the launcher.
- The launcher, a ring with your profession's icon (a bell when Craft Alert knows none yet), opens the leads window and shows, in a gold badge on its ring, how many leads you have not looked at or greeted. It glows when you hover it and pulses when a new lead arrives. It is lit while Craft Alert is listening and dim while it is paused; hover it to see why. It can hide itself while there are no leads.
- The leads window lists every open request on the left, newest first: the customer in their class colour, how long ago they asked, what they want, a dot for leads you have not looked at, and a check once greeted. Left-click a lead to see it, right-click to dismiss it; hover it for the customer's latest chat line. "Clear all" over the list dismisses every lead at once.
- The right side shows the selected lead in full: the customer, their class, channel and time, what they want, their message with hoverable links, what matched, which of your characters can craft it (in class colour, with its quality rank), whether they are on a realm you can't send a crafting order to, and the greeting that will be sent. Greet, Whisper and Dismiss buttons sit at the bottom; shift-click Greet to edit the greeting first.
- Your main crafter for a profession wins ties over the character you're playing. Choose it from a lead: left-click its crafters.
- The top of the leads list counts today's requests seen, greeted and replied to (and, on Retail, orders filled); hover it for the last 7 days. On Retail, filling a crafting order for someone you greeted in the last day counts as an order filled.
- Back from AFK, one toast says how many requests you could craft came in while you were away and how many of them expired. Left-click it to open the leads, right-click to dismiss it.
- Drag the leads window, resize it from its corner (an outline shows the new size until you let go), and close it with Escape. It keeps one size for the leads and the settings, at least 720×420.
- With WhisperMessenger installed, Craft Alert moves into it: the leads get their own tab with a count of unseen leads, the toast shows as WhisperMe
